utc: compute amendment #4 — measured infeasibility, not a scientific choice
reason: the wide nests were killed after measurement showed the storm-phase CFL cost is unaffordable: frame intervals grew 0.2 -> 29.5 -> 101.2 min as the parent's deep river stage reached the nest boundaries (dt = cfl*dx/sqrt(g*h) collapses below 1 s, ~5000 steps per simulated hour over 1.5-3M cells). Remaining work measured at 30-100+ h per nest on 4 cores.

changes.domains: corridor extents replace wide extents; RESOLUTION IS PRESERVED (6 m; pataskala 8 m) — extent was cut rather than physics resolution, the lesser compromise
changes.bc: boundary stages reconstructed from completed parent FRAMES (30-min cadence) rather than the 300 s live record, since the live record only covers the original wide perimeters; cadence limitation recorded in each BC file

scientific_justification_for_the_22h_win: the Case A vs Case B discriminator does NOT require the Aug 21 fluvial crest. The parent claimed 'I-70 impassable' at model hour 16.4 (10:25Z Aug 20). Whether that signal is real road inundation or 60 m smearing of adjacent channel water is decided AT THAT MOMENT, by comparing carriageway cells against channel cells at 6 m. That is a 0-22 h question. The separate question of whether the model can reproduce the delayed fluvial crest is already answered NEGATIVELY by the extended parent (drainage-proxy defect) and is reported as a limitation.
